first.rationale: Verify targeted pricing because competitive price pressure makes it highly consequential, while its claimed revenue lift does not by itself establish sustainable qualified revenue or downstream retention. Verify onboarding because completion and activation are both declining and its impact may offer a more durable alternative. Pending source review, run a tightly targeted, guarded promotional-pricing test for price-sensitive SMBs rather than a broad discount rollout.

mid.rationale: Run a standard experiment simplifying onboarding. The verified source shows higher completion, faster time-to-value, and improved 30-day retention, directly addressing the current declines in completion and activation while supporting sustainable qualified revenue. Do not pursue promotional pricing: its verified revenue gain came with materially worse retention.

final2.rationale: Keep the onboarding-simplification experiment. It is the only verified direction that improves completion, time-to-value, and 30-day retention, directly supporting durable revenue amid declining activation. Do not react to the competitor with promotional pricing: the verified price-sensitive SMB discount increased signups and short-term qualified revenue but reduced 30-day retention by 12%, making it a poor sustainable-response choice despite acute churn pressure. The doubled churn conversations create immediate commercial risk, but the available experimental evidence does not support discounting as the remedy.
